Monotonic Generations in Retried Workflows

A. Example, B. Sample

Abstract

Asynchronous workflows can deliver results after the product state that requested them has changed. We describe a monotonically increasing attempt generation that binds each result to a specific request state.

Our model rejects results when the stored generation differs from the job generation, even if an older child record was deleted and recreated. The generation owner remains on the aggregate root to prevent an ABA reset.

Controlled schedules demonstrate that the rule is preserved under retries, cancellation, and concurrent replacement. The fixture contains no real experimental claim; it exists to test extraction of scientific markup.
